messages:
julia-acme: Hey team — our trial credits dropped by ~45k overnight. We saw a big spike from embeddings calls around 03:00 UTC. Can you check?

sarah-support: Sorry about that — we're looking. Do you have a workspace/org id we can tie to the usage spikes?

julia-acme: Org ID: ACME-42. The usage graph shows a rapid fanout of embed requests for the nightly ingest job. It usually processes ~5k docs, last night it shows ~55k embedding calls.

sarah-support: Thanks. Tagging infra/ingest: @tony-eng @rashmi-infra. Any obvious causes? :eyes:

tony-eng: Looking. First pass: querying audit logs and job runs for ACME-42. 

ingest-bot: [automated] queued ingest-run id=run-20240315-03:00 for org=ACME-42; worker pool=ingest-v2; feature_flags={multi_embed_fanout:true}

julia-acme: We flipped that multi-embed fanout flag as part of a perf test last week — but we didn't expect a 10x multiplier. Our config only asked for a single vector per doc.

rashmi-infra: I pulled recent worker logs. There's a pattern of the same doc_id processed multiple times within the same run. Example log snippet:```
INFO 03:00:12 ingest-worker run=run-20240315-03:00 doc_id=doc-982 attempts=1 call_id=abc123
INFO 03:00:12 enqueue embed task doc_id=doc-982 idempotency_key=run-20240315-03:00:abc123
INFO 03:00:13 embed request sent doc_id=doc-982 tokens=512 status=200
INFO 03:00:14 enqueue embed task doc_id=doc-982 idempotency_key=run-20240315-03:00:abc124
INFO 03:00:14 embed request sent doc_id=doc-982 tokens=512 status=200
```
This looks like the dedupe is keyed to ephemeral call ids instead of the stable document id.

tony-eng: That aligns with a change in the fanout worker merged last week (PR #4567). The worker was meant to preserve doc_id as the idempotency key, but a refactor introduced use of run-scoped call_id for each shard. If fanout_shards > 1, each shard generates a different call_id -> duplicate embed requests.

julia-acme: So the platform sent 10 embeds for each doc because fanout_shards defaulted to 10? That would explain 5k -> 55k. :grimacing:

sarah-support: Ok — action items: 1) Stop new runs with fanout enabled for ACME-42, 2) patch worker to use stable idempotency key, 3) evaluate refund/credit remediation.

rashmi-infra: I disabled the feature flag for ACME-42 and globally set fanout_shards=1 for safety. No further embed calls after 03:06 UTC.

tony-eng: Working on a hotfix to compute idempotency_key as `org_id:doc_id:embed_type` instead of `run_id:call_id`. Draft in my branch, running unit tests. Expect patch in ~30m.

julia-acme: Thanks. Appreciate the quick containment. Can you confirm whether the extra calls were billed to our trial credits?

sarah-support: Yes — they show up against the org's usage. We can submit a credits review once engineering confirms root cause & window of duplicate calls. Please hold off refund until we have full scope.

rashmi-infra: For scope: ACME-42 had ~50k duplicate embed calls between 03:00-03:06 UTC. Average tokens per call ~480 => ~24M tokens. We'll compile exact line items.

tony-eng: Patch merged at 03:42 UTC, rolling deploy started. Also added a fallback dedupe middleware at enqueue-time to dedupe by `org:doc_id` for 24h to catch any edge cases.

sarah-support: I'll prepare the remediation package for finance (usage export, line items, suggested refund amount) and draft the customer message. Julia — we'll propose to credit back the trial tokens for the duplicate window and re-enable the flag once we confirm non-dup behavior.

julia-acme: That sounds good. Also, can you share a short mitigation checklist we can run on our side to avoid hitting prod flags accidentally? We run feature flags from our deployment script.

tony-eng: Short checklist for customers: 1) Confirm fanout_shards is intended and set to 1 for standard ingests, 2) Ensure idempotency token in client calls uses stable doc identifiers, 3) Prefer staging validation with sampling flag on a small subset. We'll also add a warning in our console when enabling multi_embed_fanout on trial orgs.

rashmi-infra: Follow-ups: monitor ACME-42 usage for next 48h, notify once credits adjusted. I've created internal incident tracking ticket: INC-2024-831.

sarah-support: Thanks everyone — I'll keep JulIa posted in-thread. Julia, expect a formal update and a proposed credit adjustment within 24 hours. :thumbsup:
